problem: Model-free RL for visual navigation is sample-inefficient and overfits to training appearance; naively adding contrastive learning to world-model RL (DreamerV2) makes encoder features collapse, because the encoder is trained on augmented views while the world model reconstructs unaugmented inputs and the policy does not train the encoder.
motivation: Robots have limited data and compute, and must generalize to unseen scenes and textures and to real-world appearance. Model-based RL is sample efficient, but its reconstruction-based latent representation does not separate task-relevant from irrelevant factors, so a robust invariant state abstraction is needed.
key_idea: Train a DreamerV2-style world model with an InfoNCE contrastive loss over style-augmented views, and prevent feature collapse with an intervention-invariant auxiliary task (e.g. depth prediction) as a regularizer.
insight: Contrastive loss alone in a world model collapses: ReCoRe-D (no depth) reaches 0.0 SR at 100k steps and 0.8 at 500k on iGibson OoD. Replacing depth with RGB reconstruction only partly recovers (19.2 SR at 500k vs 59.7). Removing contrastive loss also fails (5.0 SR at 500k). Both parts are therefore needed, and the auxiliary task must be truly invariant to the augmentation. On DMControl, segmentation as the regularizer beats denoising, since denoising is not invariant to the RGB interventions.
method: Style intervention: random spatial jitter (pad + crop), Gaussian blur, color jitter, grayscale and cutout produce two correlated views of each observation.
Invariant encoder: a 5-layer conv encoder (32 to 512 feature maps) trained with InfoNCE and a bilinear projection head; keys come from a momentum (0.999) EMA encoder as in MoCo.

Intervention-invariant regularizer: an auxiliary decoder predicts pixel-wise depth from (s_t,h_t) with negative log-likelihood. Depth is used only in training. Denoising or segmentation replace it on DMControl.
Latent dynamics: a DreamerV2 RSSM with deterministic h_t, a stochastic discrete latent, a reward head and a KL term. The total loss is L_q + L_d + L_r + βL_KL.
Controller: actor-critic trained on imagined latent rollouts (horizon 15), separate from world-model learning.
Task observation encoder: goal, position and velocities pass through two dense layers of size 32 and are concatenated with the image features.

setting.backbone: DreamerV2-based RSSM world model with a conv encoder, trained from scratch, plus actor-critic
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in iGibson (12 training scenes listed in appendix, 100k/500k env steps, textures held out); depth used as an auxiliary training target only
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (120x160) + task observation (goal location, current location, linear/angular velocity); depth only at training
setting.action_space: continuous rotation (radians) and forward distance (m) for a TurtleBot
setting.simulator: iGibson 1.0 (also Gibson scenes, DeepMind Control suite)
setting.privileged: depth ground truth during training only; goal/current location given as task observation

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 held-out scenes (Ihlen_0_int, Ihlen_1_int, Rs_int) with held-out textures

results: On iGibson OoD PointGoal, ReCoRe reaches 59.7 SR / 0.50 SPL at 500k steps, beating the strongest baseline DV2+Grounding DINO (50.0 / 0.45) and RAD (36.3). At 100k steps it is on par with DV2+G DINO (36.0 vs 37.1 SR). In sim-to-real Gibson, ReCoRe gets 71.9 SR against 60.3 for DV2+G DINO at 500k. On DMControl it beats CURL on 8 of 12 settings.
limitations: Training takes about twice as long as DreamerV2 (about 3 days on 2 RTX 3090s for 500k steps).
Needs an intervention-invariant auxiliary signal (depth or segmentation) at training time, and denoising gives limited gains.
Sim-to-real is evaluated only for the perception module in simulation with Gibson scans, with no real robot; the controller stays in the simulator.
